name: Backend (Java)
description: For Java backend engineers moving to product companies: DSA, OOP and design patterns, databases, and system design.
roadmap:
**Weeks 1-4: DSA.** Two problems a day from arrays, hashing, trees and graphs. Time yourself.
**Weeks 5-6: Java depth.** Collections internals, concurrency, JVM memory, Spring basics.
**Weeks 7-8: Databases.** Indexes, transactions and isolation levels, query plans.
**Weeks 9-10: Design.** One low-level and one system design question a week, out loud.
**Then:** a mock SDE interview and a system design mock, and fix what the scorecards say.

name: Service to product switch
description: A 12-week plan for engineers at service companies preparing for product company interviews.
roadmap:
**What changes:** product companies test problem solving live (DSA), design thinking and ownership, not only your project.
**Weeks 1-6: DSA foundations.** Patterns first (two pointers, sliding window, BFS/DFS, DP), 60-80 problems.
**Weeks 7-8: Low-level design.** Classes, SOLID, parking lot, rate limiter, LRU cache.
**Weeks 9-10: System design basics.** Load balancing, caching, databases, queues; design a URL shortener.
**Weeks 11-12: Mocks.** At least two human mock interviews; rewrite your resume around impact numbers.
**Tell your story:** why you're switching, what you owned, what you learned.

name: Frontend
description: JavaScript depth, browser fundamentals, DSA for frontend rounds and frontend system design.
roadmap:
**JavaScript:** closures, the event loop, promises, `this`, prototypes.
**Browser:** rendering, caching, HTTP, security (XSS, CSRF, CORS).
**DSA:** easy-medium problems in JavaScript; trees and recursion for DOM questions.
**Frontend system design:** design an autocomplete, a news feed, an image carousel.
